incident-bot: [PagerDuty] page fired: METR-USE-CRITICAL - metering ingestion lag + token-count drift detected for billing window

PagerDuty: Incident METR-USE-CRITICAL created and routed to on-call

Maya (on-call): acked. i'm on it. starting triage — checking ingestion/backfill status

Sam R: thx maya. quick Q: is this the same "token-count drift" we saw last month or new?

Maya (on-call): looks similar symptoms but wider. some customers show 20-40% fewer tokens in metering than raw logs. delta started ~2026-03-08 02:10 UTC per sampling

Ben (SRE): tagging in. checked kinesis -> visible backlog. consumer lag spiked at 02:08 UTC. possible consumer NACK storm or scaling flub

Alice (eng-platform): which consumer group?

Ben (SRE): consumer group = metering-aggregator-prod. consumer pods show frequent OOMs around that time in logs. image: rdinfer/meter-agg:1.14.

Maya (on-call): running quick query to estimate missing tokens per-customer:
```sql
SELECT customer_id, sum(expected_tokens) as expected, sum(recorded_tokens) as recorded, (expected - recorded) as delta
FROM metering.samples
WHERE ingest_time >= '2026-03-08 01:30:00'::timestamptz
GROUP BY customer_id
ORDER BY delta DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

Maya (on-call): top affected: cust_842, cust_1902, cust_44 — delta ranges 30k-2M tokens each. these are high-dollar customers. marking as customer-impacting (potential invoice blocker)

Billing Ops (on-call): pinged. we may need to pause invoice generation for today's window until we backfill. please provide ETA

Sam R: any quick mitigation to stop ongoing loss? can we failover to legacy aggregator?

Alice (eng-platform): we have a legacy aggregator (meter-agg-v1) in k8s in the cluster. can bring up a canary to consume Kinesis and write to the same sink. risk: duplicate writes for records already processed. need idempotency check.

Maya (on-call): plan: 1) stop new aggregator pods to prevent further NACKs 2) scale up legacy consumer with idempotency on 3) run backfill job to reprocess raw logs into metering db 4) hold billing exports until confirmed

Ben (SRE): executing step 1 now: `kubectl -n prod scale deployment metering-aggregator --replicas=0`

ops-runner: done. deployment scaled down. metrics show consumer lag stopped increasing, backlog stabilized at ~12M records

Maya (on-call): starting step 2: fire up legacy consumer with guarded write. triggering via helm: `helm upgrade --install meter-agg-legacy ./charts/meter-agg --set replicas=4 --set mode=canary`

Alice (eng-platform): set `IDEMPOTENCY=true` env in the helm values — otherwise we risk double counting

Maya (on-call): helm release applied. pods coming up. readiness failing for one pod due to env var parse; fixed, all 4 ready

Ben (SRE): legacy consumer is consuming from Kinesis now. throughput steady ~4000 rec/s. observed 2% dup avoidance in sink writes so idempotency works for sample cases

Maya (on-call): starting backfill job for window 01:30-03:30 UTC. command: `airflow dags trigger metering_backfill -c '{"start":"2026-03-08T01:30:00Z","end":"2026-03-08T03:30:00Z"}'`

Maya (on-call): backfill submitted (dag run id: backfill_20260308_01). ETA ~45-60m given data volume

Billing Ops (on-call): inserting hold on invoice export for 2026-03-08 window. flagged in billing dashboard, customers with >$1k exposed will get manual notif if we estimate impact >5%

Sam R: what about token counting code change? any recent deploys to aggregator around 02:00 UTC?

Ben (SRE): deploy history shows a rollout at 01:55 UTC for metering-aggregator (image 1.14). rollout had a brief RC and then completed. logs show repeated `MemoryError` from aggregator around 02:06 followed by pod restarts.

Maya (on-call): uploading small log sample:
```
[02:06:12] ERROR aggregator.consumer - Error processing batch: MemoryError
[02:06:12] WARN aggregator.consumer - batch retry 1/3
[02:06:13] ERROR aggregator.consumer - batch failed after retries, acking NACK to stream
```

Alice (eng-platform): probable root cause: new change in 1.14 to buffer larger batches (aimed at perf) but it increases memory. rollout didn't account for heavier cardinality months.

Ben (SRE): we need to roll back image to 1.13 immediately in prod to avoid further risk. but we already scaled aggregator to 0 — okay to keep off while legacy handles ingestion. recommend block redeploys to aggregator until postmortem

Maya (on-call): agreed. I'll file a deployment-blocker tag and update incident notes.

Billing Ops (on-call): can we estimate revenue risk now? backfill ETA 45-60m, legacy consumer now processing incoming data so future windows should be ok. current exposure quantified by your SQL?

Maya (on-call): current delta across all customers ~18M tokens (est). projected revenue impact ~ $1,900 if tokens priced at $0.00011/token; but high variance per customer. will produce final CSV after backfill

Billing Ops (on-call): ok on hold. will delay scheduled invoice export and coordinate customer comms if needed. please tag me when backfill completes

Sam R: any workaround for customers in near-term? e.g., manual ingestion of logs for top customers?

Maya (on-call): for the very top customer (cust_842) we can run targeted reprocess with narrower window. running: `python scripts/reprocess_customer.py --customer cust_842 --start 2026-03-08T01:00:00Z --end 2026-03-08T04:00:00Z`

ops-runner: reprocess job started for cust_842. logs show progress, ~10m ETA

Maya (on-call): handoff note: if anyone gets a customer-facing question before backfill finishes, tell them we're aware of lower-than-expected usage records, legacy consumer enabled, backfill running, and invoice export paused for today's window. billing ops will coordinate customer notif if impact > 5%

Ben (SRE): monitoring: backfill job progress exported to #eng-runtime metrics: backfill_progress=24% and processing rate 12k rec/s. estimated complete 38m

Sam R: pinging execs: @ceo @vp_prod - for visibility (only if needed)

Maya (on-call): cust_842 reprocess finished. delta for cust_842 reduced from 1.9M -> 5k tokens (good).

Maya (on-call): backfill progress 76% now. customers list shrinking, overall delta down to ~4.1M tokens

Billing Ops (on-call): thanks — will prepare a short note for customers with >$500 exposure. holding off wide comms until final numbers

incident-bot: PagerDuty update: METR-USE-CRITICAL escalated to SEV2 (informational) now that ingestion steady and backfill progressing

Maya (on-call): backfill complete. final delta across all customers: 12,432 tokens (within noise). closing gap confirmed via post-run SQL checks.

Alice (eng-platform): recommending permanent rollback of metering-aggregator to 1.13 and add load-sim tests for high-cardinality months. will open PR for rollback + test coverage

Ben (SRE): rollback PR merged and deploy blocked for 24h. will also add OOM alert thresholds earlier in pipeline

Billing Ops (on-call): removing invoice hold. will proceed with export and add note about transient metering gap; no invoice adjustments needed based on final numbers.

Maya (on-call): closing incident. summary: bad rollout to 1.14 increased batch memory usage -> OOMs -> consumer NACKs -> ingestion lag + token-count drift. mitigated by scaling down faulty aggregator, enabling legacy consumer with idempotency, running backfill + targeted reprocess, blocking deploys, and rolling back. Customers unaffected in final billing window.

Sam R: thanks team. please add postmortem and timeline to /oncall/incidents and assign action owners (Alice: rollback+tests, Ben: alerts, Maya: runbook update)

Maya (on-call): will start postmortem doc and ping for review.

incident-bot: Incident METR-USE-CRITICAL resolved and auto-closed by on-call after mitigation (duration ~1h 24m) :white_check_mark:
